title: What is on your card?
lead: Every element of the card: what it is and how a copy of it can be misused. Each statement is followed by the official text that says it, so you can check it yourself.

generalTitle: Why a copy of your card is risky
generalText: The Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) warns that an identity card holds more information than most checks need, and that handling it increases the risk of identity theft; a copy also does not prove who is sending it. INCIBE describes a real case in which a lost document was used to take out a loan in the victim's name. It advises never to share a copy unless it is unavoidable, and then to blur the photo, the signature and anything not relevant, and to add a watermark that says what the copy is for. The AEPD says you may hide data that is not needed to identify you, such as the support number or the issuing team.
header_what: The front shows the two-letter code of Spain, printed in negative in a blue rectangle surrounded by 12 yellow stars, and the title of the document repeated in at least one other official EU language. ICAO calls this area Zone I, the mandatory header.
header30_what: The front shows the words "Documento Nacional de Identidad", "España" and "Ministerio del Interior". ICAO calls this area Zone I, the mandatory header.
headerTie_what: The front shows the title of the document in the issuing country's language and in at least one other official EU language, and the country's three-letter code in the background printing. The card of a family member of an EU citizen who exercises free movement is outside that regulation (Art. 5); the EU rules for those residence documents are in Regulation (EU) 2025/1208.
name_what: Your surnames and given name. ICAO places them in Zone II, with the other personal data.
nameTie_what: Surnames and then forenames, in that order, with the surnames in capital letters. ICAO places them in Zone II, with the other personal data.
sex_what: Your sex. EU rules allow a country to leave it off the card. In the MRZ it is coded F (female), M (male) or < (unspecified).
sex30_what: Your sex. In the MRZ it is coded F (female), M (male) or < (unspecified).
sexTie_what: The holder's sex. In the MRZ it is coded F (female), M (male) or < (unspecified).
dniNumber_what: Your personal DNI number with its check letter. The law treats it as a general personal numeric identifier, and the letter is the check character of your tax number (NIF).
dniNumber_risk: Together with your name, this number identifies you. That is why the AEPD asks public bodies that publish an official act to show your name and only four random digits of the document, not the full number, to reduce the impact on your privacy.
nie_what: Your Foreigner Identity Number: a personal, unique and exclusive number that identifies foreign nationals. It appears on every document issued or processed for you.
nie_risk: Together with your name, this number identifies you. That is why the AEPD asks public bodies that publish an official act to show your name and only four random digits of the document, not the full number, to reduce the impact on your privacy.
supportNumber_what: The number of the physical card (the "support"), printed on the front. It is not your DNI number.
supportNumber_risk: The AEPD gives the support number as an example of data you may hide, because it is not needed to identify you.
cardNumber_what: The document number. EU rules require it in more than one place on the card, one of them with special security features.
issueDate_what: The date the card was issued.
issueDate_risk: Together with the validity date it shows how long the card lasts, and the law sets that by age at issue: 2 years under 5, 5 years from 5 to 30, 10 years from 30 to 70, and more than 10 years from 70. So the two dates reveal your age range even with the date of birth hidden.
issueDate30_what: The date the card was issued, shown in the laser image (CLI) in the format DDMMYY.
issueDate30_risk: Together with the validity date it shows how long the card lasts, and the law set that by age at issue: 2 years under 5, 5 years from 5 to 30, 10 years from 30 to 70, and permanent from 70. So the two dates reveal your age range even with the date of birth hidden.
issueDateTie_what: The date of issue, on the back, next to the place of issue.
expiryDate_what: The last day the card is valid. EU rules allow a validity of 5 to 10 years, with exceptions for minors and people aged 70 or more.
expiryDate_risk: Together with the issue date it shows how long the card lasts, which the law sets by your age when it was issued.
expiryDate30_what: The last day the card is valid.
expiryDate30_risk: Together with the issue date it shows how long the card lasts, which the law set by your age when it was issued.
expiryDateTie_what: The expiry date, always as day, month and year.
photo_what: Your digitised photo. ICAO calls it Zone V, the mandatory identification feature. On the DNI 4.0 it is larger than on earlier models.
photo_risk: INCIBE advises blurring the photo, the signature and any other information that is not relevant before you share a copy.
photo30_what: Your photo, in black and white, laser-engraved into the card. ICAO calls it Zone V, the mandatory identification feature.
photo30_risk: INCIBE advises blurring the photo, the signature and any other information that is not relevant before you share a copy.
photoTie_what: The holder's photo, built into the card body and protected by a holographic element (DOVID).
photoTie_risk: INCIBE advises blurring the photo, the signature and any other information that is not relevant before you share a copy.
signature_what: Your handwritten signature, scanned when the card was issued. ICAO calls it Zone IV.
signature_risk: INCIBE advises blurring the signature, the photo and any other information that is not relevant before you share a copy.
signatureTie_risk: INCIBE advises blurring the signature, the photo and any other information that is not relevant before you share a copy.
can_what: A six-digit number printed on the front. The Policía Nacional guide for the DNIe 3.0 chip describes it as the password for the secure contactless (NFC) connection to the chip, called PACE; the MRZ can be used instead.
can_risk: According to that guide, the connection exists so the card's data cannot be read without the holder's consent, and the Policía Nacional says the chip holds the same data printed on the card, including the photo and the signature. Whoever has your CAN has that password.
canTie_what: The card access number. ICAO sets it as six digits, in the same typeface as the MRZ.
cli_what: A laser-engraved image that changes with the viewing angle: it switches between a small ghost image of the holder and the date of issue.
window_what: A transparent window with laser engraving. On the DNI 3.0 the engraving is the support number.
window_risk: The AEPD gives the support number as an example of data you may hide, because it is not needed to identify you.
dovid_what: A holographic patch (DOVID) on the front.
dovid30_what: A kinegram: diffractive images that protect the card against photocopying.
dovidTie_what: An upgraded holographic element (DOVID) on the front, which also protects the photo.
ovi_what: Optically variable ink (OVI), whose colour changes with the viewing angle.
oviTie_what: The symbol of an electronic travel document (chip), printed in ink whose colour changes with the viewing angle.
relief_what: A raised motif on the front that you can feel with your finger.
printing_what: The background printing: guilloches, iris printing, positive and negative microtext, inks that show only under UV light, and a coded image.
printingTie_what: Secure offset background printing, UV-fluorescent printing and rainbow printing; personal data is laser-engraved.
material_what: A polycarbonate card in the ID-1 format (85.6 × 53.98 mm), 760 µm thick.
materialTie_what: A polycarbonate card in the ID-1 format.
addressTie_what: The holder's address, an optional entry on the back that must have its own heading.
placeOfBirthTie_what: The holder's place of birth, on the back.
parents_what: The given names of your parents.
team_what: The code of the police team (equipo) that issued the card.
team_risk: The AEPD gives the issuing team as an example of data you may hide, because it is not needed to identify you.
issuePlace_what: The place of issue or the issuing authority, on the back.
remarks_what: Remarks for national use, for example whether the holder may work.
permitType_what: The type of residence permit. For family members of an EU citizen who have not exercised free movement, it says "family member".
mrz_what: Three lines of 30 OCR-B characters. Line 1: document type, issuing country, document number and its check digit, optional data. Line 2: date of birth, sex, expiry date (dates as YYMMDD, each with a check digit), nationality, optional data and a final check digit. Line 3: surname, then << and the given names. Check digits use weights 7, 3, 1 modulo 10, so a reader can detect a misread character.
mrz_risk: The MRZ repeats your name, document number, date of birth and expiry date in a standard machine-readable form: hiding those fields on the front while leaving the MRZ visible gives them away. The Policía Nacional also says the MRZ can serve as the password for the contactless connection to the chip.
mrzTie_what: Three lines of 30 OCR-B characters. Line 1: document type, issuing country, document number and its check digit, optional data. Line 2: date of birth, sex, expiry date (dates as YYMMDD, each with a check digit), nationality, optional data and a final check digit. Line 3: surname, then << and the given names. Check digits use weights 7, 3, 1 modulo 10, so a reader can detect a misread character.
mrzTie_risk: The MRZ repeats the name, document number, date of birth and expiry date in a standard machine-readable form: hiding those fields on the front while leaving the MRZ visible gives them away.
chip_what: A dual-interface chip (with contacts and contactless). It stores, separately, your qualified electronic certificates and your photo, personal data and two fingerprints. According to the Policía Nacional it holds the same data printed on the card.
chip_risk: The Policía Nacional documents that contactless access to the DNIe 3.0 chip is protected by PACE, opened with the CAN or the MRZ. EU rules say only duly authorised staff may use the facial image, to verify the document or the holder.
chip30_what: A chip with an NFC antenna. It stores your personal data, the image of your photo and of your signature, a fingerprint template, and the certificates and private keys for authentication and signature.
chip30_risk: Contactless access is protected by PACE, opened with the CAN or the MRZ.
chipTie_what: A contactless chip that stores the holder's facial image and two fingerprints.
certificates_what: Qualified certificates for authentication and electronic signature, valid for two years.
certificates30_what: Certificates for authentication and electronic signature. Using them requires your PIN.
